overall_structure.value: Austenite did not decompose at 800 °C. The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy retained its austenite (FCC_A1) together with δ-ferrite (BCC_A2); no discontinuous precipitation, cellular transformation or spinodal decomposition was triggered, in agreement with the phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)) in which the austenite fraction does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C.

source.reason: The sample (9Al-10Mn-0.4C at 800 °C) is characterised by the absence of austenite decomposition at 800 °C, explained by the phase volume fraction diagram Fig. 9(a); phases listed are those predicted by that diagram.
Fig. 9(a) phase volume fraction diagram for 9Al-10Mn-0.4 shows FCC_A1 (austenite) rising steeply to ~0.49 mol at 800 °C; the text links 9Al-10Mn-0.4C to this diagram.
Fig. 9(a) phase volume fraction diagram for 9Al-10Mn-0.4 shows BCC_A2 falling to a ~0.51 mol minimum at 800 °C.
Fig. 9(a) shows KAPPA_E21 holding ~0.10 mol between 200 and 700 °C and vanishing near 850 °C for the 9Al-10Mn-0.4 composition.

simulation_method.value: CALPHAD thermodynamic equilibrium calculation (phase volume fraction / amount of all phases vs temperature)

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Equilibrium phase amounts computed for the 9Al-10Mn-0.4 composition from 0 to 1300 °C; phases BCC_A2, FCC_A1 and KAPPA_E21 tracked (Fig. 9(a)).

validation_against_experiment.value: The calculated austenite fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C, which explains the observed non-transforming behaviour of austenite at 800 °C; conversely the γ fraction drop from 1150 °C to 600 °C (Fig. 9(a)) corresponds to the discontinuous precipitation observed at 600 °C.

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy underwent austenite decomposition during tempering at 600 °C (Fig. 1(a)) but NOT at 800 °C, even though kinetics should have been faster at 800 °C; the non-transforming behaviour at 800 °C reflects the phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)), where the austenite fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C. (b0063, b0064)

No Vickers hardness or any other quantitative property data are reported for the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C composition; all hardness tables (Tables 2, 4, 5, 8, 9) cover other compositions (9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C, 12Al-30Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C), so no measured mechanical property can be attributed to this sample.

Fig. 9 contains an uncaptioned third SEM panel (20 µm scale bar) showing equiaxed grains, dark grain-boundary lines and a horizontal crack/band; its attribution to a specific composition cannot be established from the image alone and is therefore not assigned to this sample.

The general conclusion 'tempering at 800 °C triggered complete and widespread transformations like cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition' (b0117) does NOT apply to the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy, which showed no transformation at 800 °C.
